tool_args.old_string: We identify six limitations. First, although Theorem~\ref{thm:sufficient} requires only a connected design, the current evaluation achieves XX.X\% fill rate (XX{,}XXX of XX{,}XXX potential cells); sparser designs may compromise identifiability of $c_n$ for models with few observed exposed items. Relatedly, sparse observations per item produce elevated item-level mean-square residuals (92/176 items), though model- and judge-level fit remains acceptable. Second, Stage~2 exposure estimation relies on a reference model anchor (gpt-4-0314), and exposure estimate quality depends on the anchor remaining uncontaminated relative to the benchmark; as benchmarks age, anchor validity should be periodically re-assessed. Third, the current evaluation uses a single benchmark (Arena-Hard) with eight target models; post-hoc power analysis indicates that detecting $\Delta\tau = 0.071$ at $\alpha = 0.05$ requires $N \approx 17$ models for 80\% power, while $N = 8$ yields approximately 50\% power, explaining the non-significant bootstrap result. Generalization to other benchmarks and larger model populations remains to be verified. Fourth, empirical CI coverage differs by parameter type: ability estimates $\theta$ approach nominal coverage at moderate sample sizes (${\sim}$90\% at $N = 8$), while contamination susceptibility $c_n$ exhibits moderate posterior overconfidence (71\% at $N = 50$, 68\% at $N = 8$; \citealp{talts2018sbc}). The $c_n$ under-coverage reflects the multiplicative coupling $c_n \cdot e_i$ and the HalfNormal prior's boundary constraint at $c_n = 0$, which systematically narrows posterior credible intervals. Crucially, this under-coverage does not improve with sample size (68\% at $N = 8$, 71\% at $N = 50$), indicating a structural rather than finite-sample issue. Point estimates and rank orderings ($\tau = 0.857$) are unaffected; $c_n$ credible intervals should be treated as lower bounds on uncertainty, with point estimates and relative ordering serving as the primary diagnostics. SBC-based posterior recalibration \citep{talts2018sbc} and explicit modeling of the asymmetric $c_n$ posterior are directions for future work. Fifth, while self-evaluation sensitivity analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:self_eval}) confirms robust rankings when excluding self-judging observations, a more comprehensive analysis removing overlapping models entirely from the judge panel has not been conducted. Sixth, the bilinear contamination term $c_n \cdot e_i$ assumes rank-1 structure---a single latent dimension of contamination susceptibility per model. In practice, contamination may be domain-specific (e.g., coding vs.\ reasoning items), requiring a higher-rank decomposition $\sum_r c_{nr} \cdot e_{ir}$ that the current model does not capture.

```latex
LLM-as-a-judge evaluation corrects for judge bias and benchmark contamination independently, but sequential correction produces biased model ability estimates. We formalize this failure as an omitted variable bias (OVB) problem: any estimator that models one facet while omitting the other yields asymptotically biased ability estimates. We propose the Gated Many-Facet Rasch Model (G-MFRM), which jointly calibrates model ability, item difficulty, judge severity, and contamination susceptibility through staged estimation with externally anchored exposure indicators. Formal identifiability analysis proves that fixing exposure externally is both necessary and sufficient for parameter separation under standard multi-judge designs. \end{abstract}
```
